A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FingerTip 20K and its two benchmark tracks. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, model evaluations, task-difficulty experiments, and fine-tuning results in Sections 4–5, Tables 4–6, and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model comparisons, fine-tuning configurations, human studies, and generalization and ablation experiments in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The core task formulations and separately fine-tuned agents remain. Appendix A.6 adds limited procedural variants: joint training across tracks, DeepSeek-V3 summarization of relevant intents from the full history, and prediction of intent distributions instead of a single intent.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the Chinese Android benchmark with 21,437 episodes, 506 apps, and two principal tracks. v2 adds a cold-start scenario without historical intents and a multiple-suggestion probability task. The unseen-user/app/intent experiments partition existing coverage rather than introduce external datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-VL-72B and Qwen-QVQ-Max to both tracks, a human reference for suggestion, and GPT-4.1-based AutoDroid and AppAgent for execution. Qwen-QVQ-Max also replaces GPT-4.1 in the fine-tuning comparison table. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds rank-64 and 16,000-episode fine-tuning settings, held-out evaluations with retraining on 14,706 episodes, a 20-annotator/400-episode human baseline, and five-point preference ratings over 200 episodes. Its probability experiment changes success to top-three matching and revises similarity scoring. Reported collection settings also change from 91 participants and one-to-two months per participant to 95 and one month.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained screenshot-count and action-length analyses, v2 adds training-size/rank sensitivity, unseen-user/app/intent tests, cross-track and joint-training comparisons, history/context ablations, probability-output analysis, human validation of Sim2, and a control excluding identical historical tasks. These address several previously untested mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added user-rating averages and predicted intent distributions do not introduce uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: Matched original baseline and 1,000-episode/rank-4 fine-tuning scores remain unchanged. v2 adds extensive results, including Qwen-QVQ-Max's 12.8% suggestion success and the 16,000-episode/rank-64 model's 26.0% suggestion and 15.5% execution success; these are new configurations, not same-setting gains. Tables 8–14 add supplementary outcomes, and the validation category count changes from 0 to 27.

T1.justification: The principal task equations and metric definitions remain unchanged. Appendix A.6.5 introduces a time-conditioned distributional target constructed from clustered intents and redefines success and similarity for that target. This is a limited mathematical-definition extension, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark, longitudinal data, two-track novelty, and benefits of user-oriented fine-tuning remain the central contributions. v2's abstract and introduction additionally claim a substantial human–agent capability gap, supported by its newly reported human study.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generalization, negative cross-track transfer, the importance of history and time, agreement between Sim2 and user preferences, and possible reuse of identical tasks. Its limitations no longer state that generalization was untested or training used only 1,000 episodes. Appendix A.3 also discusses realistic interaction noise and regional applicability.

D1.justification: v2 documents participant demographics, quality and privacy checks, training-set selection, and construction of the new experimental variants and human studies. It directs code and data access to GitHub instead of the anonymous-code and Kaggle links. Conversely, v1's Qwen-VL-Max/PaddleOCR action-repair recipe disappears. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish when the underlying collection procedures changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds AppAgent and AutoDroid references and includes AndroidWorld in the related-work comparison table, while removing SmartAgent and several peripheral references. The central positioning around longitudinal user context and proactive/personalized mobile interaction remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and selected explanatory passages, standardizes terminology, adds affiliation and conference information, and introduces ethics and reproducibility statements. Data splits move from Section 4.5 to Appendix A.5. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are substantially redesigned, Table 1 is reorganized around user-defined tasks, contextual information, and historical data, and the main result tables expand. Seven supplementary result tables are added. Figures and tables are resized or relocated throughout the new conference layout; the original quantitative plots are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential foundation. Appendix A.6 addresses v1's explicitly untested generalization, adds human evidence for the personalization metric, and tests context dependence and possible reuse of identical tasks. Expanded baselines and training-scale experiments further improve assessment of the benchmark. These gains outweigh the loss of the action-repair documentation, although uncertainty remains unreported and the human–model comparison uses different test-set sizes.
